chunks: It is narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said:

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام would say in the latter part of his Witr, while standing: “My Lord, I have done evil and wronged myself, and wretched is what I have done, and these are my two hands as recompense for what they have done.”
He said: then he would stretch out both his hands together before his face and say: “And this is my neck, humbled before You for what it has brought.”

He said: then he would lower his head and humble his neck, then say: “And here I am before You, so take for Yourself from my soul that by which You are satisfied, until You are pleased. To You belongs the return in reproach; I will not return, I will not return, I will not return.”
He said: and by Allah, when he said, “I will not return,” he did not return.

key_terms.الْعُتْبَى: the return in repentance and seeking restored pleasure after blame
key_terms.رَبِّ: My Lord; direct address to Allah in supplication
key_terms.رَقَبَتِي: my neck; symbol of submission and humility before Allah
key_terms.ظَلَمْتُ: I wronged; admission of wrongdoing against oneself
key_terms.لَا أَعُودُ: I will not return; firm resolve not to go back to sin
key_terms.وَتْرِهِ: his Witr prayer, the odd-unit night prayer

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام say in the qunūt of Witr prayer about repentance and not returning to sin?
ai.summary: This hadith records a supplication of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام in the Witr prayer, expressing confession of sin, humility, and complete submission before Allah. It highlights sincere tawbah, bodily humility in du'a, and the Imam’s truthfulness in resolving never to return to sin.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1410 - It is narrated by Abu Hamzah al-Thumali that

Imam Ali ibn al-Hussain (as) would say in the last part of his Witr prayer while standing:
Rabbi as’atu wa zhalamtu nafsi wa bi’sa ma sana‘tu wa hadhihi yadayya jaza’an bima sana‘ata
"My Lord (azj), I have committed wrongs and wronged myself, and what a terrible thing I have done. Here are my hands as recompense for what they have done."

Then he would raise both his hands before his face and say:
Wa hadhihi raqabati khadi‘atun laka lima atat
"And here is my neck, humbled before You for what it has done."

He would then bow his head and humble his neck and continue:
Wa ha ana dha bayna yadayka fakhudh linafsika ar-rida min nafsi hatta tarda. Laka al-‘utba, la a‘ood, la a‘ood, la a‘ood
"Here I am before You; take from my soul the satisfaction that pleases You until You are content. To You belongs all repentance. I will not return, I will not return, I will not return [to sin]."
It is reported that by Allah (swt), when He said: "I will not return," he never returned [to the sin].
